expansion:
A is correct. A penetrating open-globe injury with a retained metallic intraocular foreign body has a high risk of intraocular infection; prompt intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics before definitive repair to reduce the risk of post-traumatic endophthalmitis (not taken from the course material). The scenario is clearly within the lecture’s open-globe/IOFB pathway: hammering is a suspicious history, and an IOFB “suggests globe penetration” (L25, slide 52/50; L25, slide 52). CT is also the appropriate imaging modality for locating a metallic IOFB (L25, slide 52).

There is a course-material gap relevant to the keyed intervention: L25 does not state that intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotics should be given for an open globe with an IOFB. Its immediate measures are instead to “Place EYE SHIELD & CALL for OPHTHALMOLOGIST immediately,” keep the patient NPO for general anaesthesia, and avoid pressure or further examination (L25, slide 51). These urgent protective measures should accompany systemic antimicrobial treatment; the lecture specifically says that no eye drops or ointment should be used on an open globe (L25, slide 51).

B is wrong because topical corticosteroid drops are not the initial treatment for an open globe. They are topical eye drops, whereas the lecture directs “No further eye exam or eye drops or ointment on an open globe” (L25, slide 51). They do not provide the required systemic antimicrobial prophylaxis (not taken from the course material).

C is wrong because topical pilocarpine is also an eye drop and must not be instilled into an open globe (L25, slide 51). It has no role in preventing infection after a penetrating injury with an IOFB (not taken from the course material).

D is wrong because intravenous mannitol is used to lower raised intraocular pressure, not as routine initial treatment for a penetrated globe with an IOFB (not taken from the course material). The lecture explicitly says not to check eye pressure in suspected open globe injury (L25, slide 51), so there is no stated indication here for pressure-lowering treatment.
objective: A confirmed penetrating open-globe injury with a retained metallic IOFB requires prompt intravenous broad-spectrum antibiotic prophylaxis before surgery.
